additions.reason: Torah is the central concept of the teaching and the dominant node of Package 1. The Rebbe opens: 'ki haTorah hi ruchaniyut' — Torah IS spirituality. This is the foundational bechina of the entire teaching: Torah's essential nature is spiritual, not physical. The teaching circles this identity throughout all 6 lines and concludes with it: 'ki davar ruchani eino tofes makom'. Torah is the hub connecting to both ruchaniyut (explicitly: 'Torah IS ruchaniyut') and sekhel ruchani (a spiritual intellect can hold all of Torah). Torah also appears in the negative framing ('divrei haTorah' that get materialized) but as the object of the evil action, not as a node in Package 2 — Torah itself belongs to the good cluster, while the danger is materializing it.

additions.reason: Ruchaniyut (spirituality) is the second node of Package 1, explicitly identified with Torah ('Torah IS ruchaniyut') and with the property of taking no space ('davar ruchani eino tofes makom'). The Rebbe uses ruchaniyut as a technical term for the essential quality of Torah — not a metaphor but an ontological identity. The teaching presents ruchaniyut as the enabling condition of limitless Torah retention: because Torah is spiritual, a spiritual intellect can hold all of it without displacement. Ruchaniyut is also the mirror-opposite of gashmiyut (Package 2) — the two are the same axis of existence, one orientation holy and one deficient.

The sekhel ruchani is characterized by 'zakh yashar po'olo' (pure and straight in his deeds) — the purity that allows spiritual identity. This concept is the positive human embodiment of the Torah-Ruchaniyut identity.

additions.reason: The quality of taking no space ('eino tofes makom') is the Rebbe's definitional property of spirituality — it appears twice in the teaching (lines 2 and 6) as the axiomatic reason Torah can be fully retained when treated spiritually. This is not an eitza consequence of ruchaniyut but its essential DEFINITION: what it means to be ruchani IS to be without spatial limit. The phrase appears as the conclusive explanation in both the opening argument ('davar ruchani eino tofes makom') and the closing proof ('ki davar ruchani eino tofes makom') — making it a structural bechina of ruchaniyut, not a result from it. additions.reason: Mamashut (substance/materiality) is the dominant node of Package 2 and the conceptual antithesis of Torah's ruchaniyut. The word appears 5 times in the teaching (lines 3-6) and is the etymological source of the teaching's key word 'yamush' ('yamush — mileshon mamashut'). When Torah is made into mamashut ('oseh mimena mamashut'), it becomes subject to spatial limits — but this limit (shiyur ve-kitzba) is an eitza consequence, not a bechina node. Mamashut is explicitly paired with gashmiyut twice as synonymous concepts ('mamashut ve-gashmiyut' in lines 4 and 5), establishing their shared essential nature through repeated coupling. Mamashut is also the warning target in the verse's reinterpretation: 'lo yamush — hizaher shelo tihyeh mamashut ve-gashmiyut be-divrei haTorah' — the entire practical instruction of the Torah is to prevent mamashut. This is Package 2's dominant node: highest frequency, etymological root of yamush, and the concept around which the entire negative teaching orbits.

The Rebbe uses 'mamashut ve-gashmiyut' as a compound concept, treating both as expressions of the same essential quality — the physical, space-occupying, limit-bound nature of things. Gashmiyut is the evil mirror of ruchaniyut (Package 1): just as Torah's essential nature IS ruchaniyut, its antithesis (when materialized) IS gashmiyut. The Rebbe also uses the verbal form 'megashem divrei haTorah' (materializing Torah's words) in line 3 — the root gashot/gashem appears as both noun and verb, emphasizing its role as the active process of making spiritual things physical. The act of 'meghasshem' and the result 'gashmiyut' are the same essential phenomenon.

additions.reason: Yamush is the key word of the teaching's verse ('lo yamush sefer haTorah hazeh mipicha') and the Rebbe explicitly derives its meaning from mamashut: 'yamush — mileshon mamashut' (yamush is from the language/root of mamashut). This is a classic bechina-by-etymology: the essential nature of the word yamush IS mamashut — departure from the mouth IS materialization. The proof-text cited ('vayamesh choshekh' — the tangible/felt darkness of Egypt) confirms that the root yod-mem-shin means 'palpable, touchable, material' — precisely mamashut. The verse's warning is therefore reinterpreted: 'lo yamush' does not mean 'should not depart' in the simple sense, but 'should not be made mamashut/material'. This is a bechina of the word's meaning with its essential conceptual nature — yamush IS an expression of mamashut.

eitza_nodes_excluded.reason: Forgetting is explicitly an eitza consequence: 'u'mizeh BA hashikhah' — from materialization COMES (ba) forgetting. The word 'ba' (comes/comes from) is the classic eitza marker. Forgetting is what mamashut PRODUCES, not what it IS. It flows FROM Package 2 as a consequence but is not a bechina member of it. Not assigned to any package.

The sustaining of learning ('yitkayem talmmudo') is the eitza result when Torah remains spiritual: 'va'azai yitkayem talmmudo' — and THEN the learning will be sustained. The 'va'azai' (and then) is eitza language. It flows FROM Package 1 as a benefit but is not a bechina member of it. Not assigned to any package.

Measure and limit: 'yesh lah shiyur ve-kitzba' — mamashut GIVES Torah a spatial limit. This is an eitza consequence of materializing Torah, not a parallel-nature identity with mamashut. The 'yesh lah' phrasing (there is to it / it has) indicates a property attributed by causal action, not a shared essential nature. Not assigned to any package.

Rav Yosef appears only as a historical proof-case in the Talmudic story (Bava Metzia 85), not as a conceptual node with bechina relationships. He fasted to sustain his learning — the story illustrates the teaching's principle but does not add new bechina concepts. Not assigned to any package.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The darkness of Egypt (Exodus 10:21) is cited only as a linguistic proof that the root yod-mem-shin means 'palpable/material' (mamashut). It is a scriptural proof-text for the etymological bechina yamush → mamashut. The darkness itself is not a conceptual node in Torah #110 — it is external scriptural evidence, not an internal teaching element. Excluded.

The word 'picha' (your mouth) in the verse is interpreted in line 5: 'mipicha — kelo'mar mekhamat pikha, sheyotze me'itkha, yihyeh la mamashut ve-gashmiyut, tizaher mizeh.' The mouth is the site where Torah can become mamashut — it is the medium of the eitza (the means by which materialization occurs in speech), not a bechina node. The mouth belongs to the eitza layer, not the bechina layer. Excluded.

Torah study is the practice that the teaching addresses, but it is not a separate bechina node from תורה itself. The teaching's subject is Torah — its retention or forgetting. Torah study is subsumed under the dominant node 'תורה'. Not a separate addition.
